Hi Avery / Samir — thanks again for taking time this morning. Quick recap from our discovery and proposed next steps so we have alignment before building the POC plan.

Key business objectives you shared:
- Safely power clinical note summarization and triage for after-hours team (target: 20k notes/day).
- Maintain PHI controls and auditability for regulatory reviews.
- Keep inference cost below $0.02 per note at 90% of throughput.

Proposed POC scope (initial):
1) Ingest sample of 5k historical notes (anonymized) -> run summarization model -> measure latency, accuracy against baseline set of 300 hand-labeled cases.
2) Validate end-to-end network/data flow for the two hosting options you prioritized: Hosted (Redwood-managed) and Private VPC (customer-managed).
3) Confirm cost model and autoscaling behavior at 5k/10k/20k concurrent notes.

Success criteria (draft) — please edit: See attached Celsia-POC-Success-Criteria.xlsx for the scoring matrix, but headline targets:
- Latency: median < 800ms per note at 95th percentile traffic pattern
- Quality: Rouge-L/Accuracy >= 88% vs label set (no major regression from baseline)
- Security: audit logs available, KMS integration validated, and no PII egress issues
- Cost: projected per-note unit cost <= $0.02 at steady-state 20k/day

Decision needed from Celsia: hosting mode for the POC (hosted sandbox vs dedicated sandbox vs VPC trial). My recommendation for POC speed is Hosted sandbox with a VPC follow-on for final security validation. Hosted gets you running in ~5 business days; VPC will take ~3–4 weeks for networking and certs.

Next steps I propose:
- You: confirm success criteria and choose hosting preference by EOD Tue (16 Jan).
- Redwood: we build a detailed POC plan + timeline and share a mutual action plan (MAP) by Wed 17 Jan.
- Loop in procurement for any MSA/NDA items if procurement wants a paper path.

Attachments: success criteria workbook, hosted vs VPC one-pager, SOC2 notes.

Thanks — Ben

--

Avery / team — technical notes for the POC environment options so you have clarity for procurement/security: 

Hosted sandbox (fastest):
- Redwood-managed compute, ephemeral customer tenant, standard SOC2 controls across our hosted environment. Recommended for initial functional validation.
- KMS: Redwood-managed keys optional. Logs and audit trails available via Console export.
- Expected ramp: 3 business days to provision + ingestion.

Dedicated sandbox (reserved capacity):
- Dedicated GPU pool for Celsia with isolated tenancy. Provides predictable throughput for load testing but requires a short capacity allocation window (typically 5–7 business days).
- Better for stress testing to reach 20k/day with stable p95 latency.

VPC trial (customer-managed networking):
- Best fit for security/compliance validation. Requires cross-team coordination (network, firewall rules, certs). Estimated 3–4 weeks.
- We support KMS integrations (bring-your-own-key) and HSM-based flows for production.

Implementation detail: for hosted sandbox perf we recommend starting with a gpt-small-optimized variant and enabling prefix caching — this keeps cost low while we measure quality. If we see skew, we can swap to a quantized medium and rerun metrics.

I'll prepare a short tech appendix for the MAP with ports, cert endpoints, and sample Docker images for the VPC side.

-Rishi

Redwood Inference
